stem: Which statement best describes nursing peer review?

options.A: It is the manager's annual employment-performance appraisal focused on attendance, goals, compensation, and job performance.
options.B: It is informal coworker feedback that is not intended to assess nursing practice against professional standards.
options.C: It is a systematic assessment by nursing peers of the quality and appropriateness of nursing care against professional standards of practice.
options.D: It is the credentialing process used to verify an applicant's education and license before employment.

rationale: ANA describes nursing peer review as a process in which practicing registered nurses systematically assess, monitor, and make judgments about the quality of nursing care provided by peers as measured against professional standards of practice. The focus is nursing practice and quality improvement, accountability, learning, and identification of practice patterns needing improvement. Therefore C is correct. A describes employment performance evaluation, B describes informal peer feedback, and D describes credential verification rather than peer review.
educational_objective: Differentiate nursing peer review from performance appraisal, informal peer feedback, and credentialing by recognizing its systematic assessment of peer nursing practice against professional standards.
source_document_title: Peer Review Tip: Distinguishing the Difference Between Peer Review, Peer Evaluation, and Peer Feedback
source_version_date: ANA consultation article originally published April 2015; current ANA page live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: Peer review section: practicing RNs systematically assess, monitor, and make judgments about quality of nursing care provided by peers as measured against professional standards; focus of peer review is practice, including quality, strengths/weaknesses, evidence for practice change, and patterns requiring more knowledge.
source_claim_supported: Nursing peer review is a systematic peer assessment of nursing-care quality and appropriateness against professional standards, distinct from employment performance evaluation, casual feedback, or credentialing.

source_original.stem: Which statement best describes nursing peer review?

options.A: Peer review is the manager’s annual employment-performance appraisal of a nurse’s attendance, goals, and job performance.
options.B: Peer review is informal feedback between coworkers that is not intended to assess practice against professional standards.
options.C: Nursing peer review is a systematic assessment by nursing peers of the quality and appropriateness of nursing care against professional standards.
options.D: Peer review is the credentialing process used to verify an applicant’s initial education and licensure before employment.

source_original.rationale: ANA describes nursing peer review as a systematic assessment by practicing registered nurses of the quality of nursing care provided by peers against professional standards. It is intended to support accountability, learning, and practice improvement rather than function as a purely punitive process.
source_original.source_detail: Definition and purpose of nursing peer review Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. correction_summary: Retained the peer-review construct and key C, tightened distractors to clearly distinguish peer review from performance appraisal, informal feedback, and credentialing, and reduced difficulty from hard to medium because the final item tests a direct professional-practice definition.

audit_findings.source_authority: Current ANA professional-practice guidance; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: ANA Peer Review Tip remains live/current and was rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: ANA article peer review definition, focus, and distinction from peer evaluation/feedback
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item mirrors ANA's systematic peer-practice assessment definition and does not mischaracterize peer review as punitive, managerial appraisal, or credentialing.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because managerial performance appraisal is distinct from peer review.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because informal peer feedback is distinct from systematic review against standards.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because credential verification is not peer review.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C includes systematic peer assessment of nursing-care quality against professional standards.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe professional evaluation processes and are parallel in scope.
